text.p: Borussia Dortmund player profiles for Wednesday's European Cup final against Juventus:
Stefan Klos, goalkeeper, 25. Not the largest of 'keepers at 1.82 metres but has turned into one of Dortmund's key players since he joined in 1988. An under-21 international.

Matthias Sammer, libero, 29. One of Germany's most influential players during last year's European championship triumph. European footballer-of-the-year. He has a reputation for being good at going forward as well as defending but his match fitness has been hit hard by injuries in recent weeks. Used to play in Italy with Internazionale Milan.

Juergen Kohler, defender, 31. Germany's most experienced defender had said he would quit the international game after bowing out of Euro 96 with injury but has changed his mind and may go on to the next World Cup finals. Key man-to-man marker. Joined in 1995 after successful spell at Juventus. Played for Italians when they beat Dortmund in 1993 UEFA Cup final.
Martin Kree, defender, 32. Former Bayer Leverkusen player has nothing like the same amount of experience as Kohler but was impressive in semifinal against Manchested United.

Paul Lambert, midfielder, 27. Scotland international who joined on a free transfer from Motherwell at start of season. One of least experienced players in the team at international level but has produced some impressive performances in defensive midfield role domestically and in European Cup.

Stefan Reuter, wing-back, 30. An important part of German national team at Euro 96. One of the fastest players in the game, he usually operates down the right but is flexible enough to take on the libero role on occasions. A former Bayern Munich player, he also came to Dortmund from Juventus in 1992.
Joerg Heinrich, wing-back, 27. Slight but swift German international who operates on the left-hand side. Came from Freiburg in 1995 and has played for national side.

Andy Moeller, midfielder, 29. German international and another former Juventus player who suffered many ups and downs in his career. Major disappointment at 1994 World Cup but bounced back at Euro 96. Moeller is the key playmaker who can also score spectacular goals. Was a big hit during his days at Juventus and played for the Italians against Dortmund in 1993 UEFA Cup final.

Lars Ricken, midfielder, 20. Burst into the first team while still at school and has had to combine his studies with professional football. He has ability to go forward and has scored crucial goals in Europe.

Paulo Sousa, midfielder, 26. Experienced Portugese international who has been suffering with calf injury lately. Came from Juventus in 1996 and has a lot to prove to the Italians where he struggled to make an impact because of injury.
Stephane Chapuisat, forward, 27. Swiss international who has a reputation for scoring goals but also for being a tough customer despite his relatively small frame.
Karlheinz Riedle, striker, 31. Former Lazio player who used to be major figure in German national team but has been hampered by injuries in last few seasons. Has been in good form lately.
